units.scopeRationale: The main explanation defines RTO and contrasts RPO; wrong feedback distinguishes MTTR. This is 5.2 recovery-metric support after an answer, not fresh evidence or a lesson on architecture.

reviewedText.exp: RTO is the target time to restore an acceptable service level. RPO instead concerns tolerable data loss; neither guarantees successful recovery.

wrongFeedback.0: Backup frequency is related to RPO (Recovery Point Objective), not RTO.
wrongFeedback.2: The amount of acceptable data loss is the RPO (Recovery Point Objective). RTO concerns restoration TIME.
wrongFeedback.3: Average repair duration is MTTR, whereas the RTO is the planned restoration target for this service.

delivery.conditions: Select an eligible set containing m032 in main MCQ practice, select an answer and submit; user.tier must equal pro to show current.exp. Selected wrong-choice feedback additionally requires a wrong submitted choice. The complete bundle is not displayed at once.

units.scopeRationale: The explanation identifies BIA and distinguishes its outputs from continuity, recovery and incident plans. This supports 5.2 BIA; mentioning an IRP does not teach 4.8 incident-response processes.

reviewedText.exp: A BIA identifies critical functions and disruption impacts. Its findings inform continuity planning and recovery targets such as RTO and RPO.

wrongFeedback.0: A DRP focuses on recovering IT systems after a disaster — it uses the outputs from the BIA.
wrongFeedback.2: A BCP defines HOW operations will continue — it is the plan built from BIA findings.
wrongFeedback.3: An IRP guides responses to security incidents — not broad operational disruptions.

delivery.conditions: Select an eligible set containing m086 in main MCQ practice, select an answer and submit; user.tier must equal pro to show current.exp. Selected wrong-choice feedback additionally requires a wrong submitted choice. The complete bundle is not displayed at once.

units.scopeRationale: The explanation checks a four-hour RPO against three-hour versioned backups and warns that replication can copy deletion. This supports 5.2 RPO and 3.4 backup frequency/recovery/replication. The second code follows from actual backup reasoning, not parent question or deck tags.

reviewedText.exp: Three-hour versioned backups meet the four-hour RPO if backups and restoration work. Replication without history may copy the deletion instead of preserving a recoverable version.

wrongFeedback.0: Weekly backups can lose days of changes, exceeding a four-hour recovery-point target.
wrongFeedback.1: Daily backups can leave nearly 24 hours between recoverable points, exceeding the target.
wrongFeedback.3: Replication can copy the deletion. Without retained history, it provides no earlier recoverable version.

delivery.conditions: Select an eligible set containing m088 in main MCQ practice, select an answer and submit; user.tier must equal pro to show current.exp. Selected wrong-choice feedback additionally requires a wrong submitted choice. The complete bundle is not displayed at once.

units.scopeRationale: The explanation distinguishes the outer business interruption limit from RTO and contrasts RPO/MTTR. Propose 5.2 supporting BIA/continuity context only; MTD is not an explicit named exam bullet.

reviewedText.exp: MTD is the outer tolerable interruption limit. RTO targets restoration early enough to support business recovery within that limit.

wrongFeedback.0: RPO concerns the acceptable age of recovered data, not the total tolerable business interruption.
wrongFeedback.2: RTO is the restoration target used in recovery planning, not the entire outer business tolerance window.
wrongFeedback.3: MTTR measures average repair time, not the maximum interruption the business can tolerate.

delivery.conditions: Select an eligible set containing m196 in main MCQ practice, select an answer and submit; user.tier must equal pro to show current.exp. Selected wrong-choice feedback additionally requires a wrong submitted choice. The complete bundle is not displayed at once.

units.scopeRationale: The explanation distinguishes a service-restoration target from data-loss tolerance, average repair and annual frequency. Propose 5.2 RTO metric support; a contrast alone does not assign a new topic or secondary mastery.

reviewedText.exp: RTO targets service-restoration time within the tolerable interruption. RPO measures data-loss tolerance instead.

wrongFeedback.0: RPO concerns acceptable data loss measured backward from disruption, not service restoration duration.
wrongFeedback.2: MTTR is an average repair-duration measure, not this specified recovery target.
wrongFeedback.3: ARO estimates event frequency per year rather than recovery time.

units.scopeRationale: The table defines and contrasts RTO, RPO, MTTR and MTBF. All four are 5.2 BIA metrics. The complete table is a support unit; it has no MTD row or BIA-process teaching. Parent physical-security/asset/hardening objectives are not supported by this table.

rows: Target time to restore an acceptable service level
A guarantee that recovery will finish on time
Maximum targeted period of data loss measured backward from disruption
How long the outage may last
Average time to repair or restore
Average operating time between repairable failures
The lifetime of a non-repairable item
